messages:
kevin: Heads up — saw a spike of streaming reconnects yesterday that fell back to cpu variants. Console just shows 'fallback' with no reason, so support + billing are confused.

maya: Yup. Affected a couple of mid-market tenants. Billing shows token consumption up even though latency SLOs held. My guess: missing telemetry tag.

li: Can you share an event id/sample log?

kevin: event id ev_2026-03-20_17:12:01, sample log: `route=us-east primary=gpu-rtx512 fallback=cpu-quantized reason=proxy_timeout request_id=abc123`. We emit `reason` but console doesn't surface it.

ram: Looks like dashboards only use `container_type` and `model_variant`. We never indexed `fallback_reason`. :thinking_face: 

maya: Confirmed. routing-service emits reason but the kafka->metrics transformer drops unknown fields because we're still on schema v1.

li: Short-term mitigation — routing service can emit a dedicated fallback annotation on resume/close events, like header `x-fallback-reason: proxy_timeout`, so console/traces can pick it up without changing metrics pipeline.

kevin: Fine for short-term, but we need a proper fix in telemetry. Also: ensure quota/billing doesn't double-count (gpu_quota should not increment when traffic gets CPU-fallback).

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary started for routing-service patch (prod-us-east) — ver 2.14.7-canary, 5% traffic.

ram: Billing pipeline reads `resource_id` and `model_variant`. Adding `fallback_reason` as a raw dimension will spike cardinality. We should enum-ize.

maya: Agreed. Proposal: keep `fallback_reason` in logs/traces verbatim, but in metrics map to coarse buckets only: `proxy_timeout`, `overloaded`, `oom`, `fallback_other`.

li: Sounds good. Plan: routing-service emits enum reason; telemetry pipeline maps to `fallback_reason_bucket`. Console will show a small pill on request details and allow filtering by bucket on the stream timeline.

kevin: Action items: @ram update metrics schema + dashboards, @maya push routing-service enum + kafka schema bump, @li add console pill + filter. Target: canary -> 20% tomorrow, full rollout Thurs. Any concerns?

ram: No objections. I'll open the PRs and add migration notes for dashboards (will need to edit a few saved queries).

maya: PR opened: https://git.company/repo/pull/789 — adds enum, kafka schema bump, and emits `x-fallback-reason` header for traces. Note: can't backfill historical events.

li: Console UI PR #456 ready for review — adds `Fallback: <bucket>` pill in request inspector and a `Fallback reason` filter on timeline. Feature-flagged under `ui.fallback_reason`.

kevin: :thumbsup: Also create an alert: fallback-rate > 2% sustained for 5m. We want early ops visibility.

ops-bot: alerting-bot: Created alert rule `fallback-rate-high` (threshold 2% / 5m) in prod-us-east.

maya: One more ask — billing team: please confirm that moving CPU-fallback traffic will not inflate GPU capacity chargebacks. @billing-team

ram: I'll coordinate with billing. Plan: map cpu-fallback events to `fallback_cpu` resource_id so quota meters distinguish it.

kevin: Thanks all. After rollout let's add a small dashboard tile showing fallback_reason distribution and anchor it on the SLO dashboard.

maya: Noted. I'll add a dashboard PR after metrics schema lands.

li: We'll also add a tooltip in the console explaining the difference between fallback buckets (to reduce support noise).

kevin: Cool. Closing loop — ping here once canary -> 20% is done.
